answer: Each identity must pass a jury-graded writing challenge, so original judgment, not electricity or capital, is the scarce resource. An attacker running N fakes must write N distinct answers every epoch, so cost grows linearly with N, while jurors spot copies, like flaws in an opal, and slash them. Reputation forms a ridge: new identities earn little until proven, and a ledge cap on early rewards makes mass-minting unprofitable.
